clue.text: Eccentric man from Wales

parts.note: in engineering an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel that turns rotation into back-and-forth motion
a man's name, a typical crossword chap

explanation.surface: An oddball Welshman, the sort of character every village is said to have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective describing the man, but it is a noun from engineering, and the man is just a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the old Latin name for Wales, so the adjective describes a person or thing native to that country.

clue.text: Carriage cut the end off Chesterfield's leg

indicators.note: cutting off the end means the final letter of the word in front is dropped

parts.note: a cabriolet is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone sawing a bit off the leg of a Chesterfield sofa, or the carriage of a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chesterfield is a deep-buttoned leather sofa; a cabriole leg is the curved S-shaped leg found on such furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture makers call the curving, outward-bowed support a cabriole, so it names the kind of leg on that sofa.

clue.text: Growth on the face is bound to hurt without an opiate at first

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: bound to do something means you must

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of opiate
to hurt is to ache

explanation.surface: A grim warning that a facial growth will be painful unless some drug is given first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here is the old word for outside, not 'lacking', so the drug's initial goes in rather than being left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a classic example of something growing on someone's face.

clue.text: Stand upright, say, on the stair

definitions.text: Stand upright, say, on the stair

parts.note: surface reading: an instruction to get to your feet, perhaps on a staircase
setter's reading: the vertical board that stands upright between one tread and the next

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a command to stand up straight; it is really describing a piece of a staircase that stands upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Joiners give that name to the vertical face of each step, the part rising between consecutive treads.

clue.text: Credit a Jewish writer of old

parts.note: taken as written
the scribes were the scholars and copyists of the law in ancient Judaism

explanation.surface: Giving acknowledgement to an ancient Jewish author.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to someone is to attribute it to them, as in crediting a quotation to an author.

clue.text: Radio operator is getting glowing reports!'.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the traditional nickname for a ship's wireless operator
second meaning: hot specks flying off with a crack

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a radio man receiving praise; here 'glowing' means literally hot and 'reports' means bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Early wireless sets worked by spark gaps, hence the nickname, and fiery particles that glow and crackle share the same plural word.

clue.text: Certainly not a plebeian girl, going on the name

parts.note: a girl's name
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that a girl is no commoner, judging by her name.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the aristocratic class stood opposite the common people, so a noble is the reverse of a commoner.

clue.text: Heartless teacher, head of divinity, is fanatical

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of divinity

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted religious teacher, perhaps a head of divinity, is a zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the middle B of RABBI to leave RABI, then add D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid literally describes a dog with rabies, and figuratively a person with violently extreme views.

clue.text: Discover gnome's pastime

parts.note: to discover is to see or find out
a gnome is a pithy saying, and so is a saw

explanation.surface: Uncovering what garden gnomes do for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A gnome here is not a garden ornament but an old word for a maxim or aphorism.
explanation.definitionFit: Children going up and down on a balanced plank is a playground amusement, which suits the word for a recreation.

clue.text: Admission that regulation eggs are going up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a regulation is a law
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Confessing that controlled egg prices are rising.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or confession, so it is a kind of admission of something.

clue.text: Sportsmen in the Royal Horse Guards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge, a Blue is someone who has represented the university at a sport
second meaning: the regiment's traditional nickname

explanation.surface: Athletes serving in a cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British: an Oxbridge sporting award, and the nickname of a cavalry regiment, now the Blues and Royals.
explanation.definitionFit: University athletes awarded colours are known by that word, and the cavalry regiment was nicknamed for its blue tunics.

clue.text: Chap with a supply of food that could be envied

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
a good table is the food someone provides, as in 'keeps a fine table'

explanation.surface: A man with plenty to eat is someone others might be jealous of.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to envy or desire what another has, so the adjective describes something worth envying.

clue.text: Question execution of snow scene

indicators.note: an execution here is a beheading, so the first letter is chopped off

parts.note: a snowy scene is a winter view

explanation.surface: Wondering about how a wintry picture was painted or carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' suggests carrying out a painting, but it means a beheading: take the W off WINTER VIEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to put questions to them, so the verb matches questioning.

clue.text: Had Mrs. Gandhi no right in this country?

definitions.text: Had Mrs. Gandhi no right in this country?

indicators.note: no right means a letter standing for right is removed

parts.note: Indira Gandhi, prime minister

explanation.surface: A political question about whether Mrs Gandhi had any rights in her nation.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the usual abbreviation for right; remove it from her first name. The whole clue also describes the country she led.
explanation.definitionFit: Indira Gandhi was prime minister of that South Asian nation, so the whole question points to her homeland.

clue.text: Holes in delicate fabric worn by girl

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone goes around them, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wearing lace that has holes in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Una is a girl's name from Spenser's Faerie Queene, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are gaps or missing portions, especially in a text, so they are holes in a broad sense.

clue.text: He set courses for Prince Henry

definitions.text: He set courses for Prince Henry

parts.note: surface reading: someone arranging the dishes of a meal, or the lessons of a curriculum, for a prince
setter's reading: the title by which the fifteenth-century Portuguese prince is remembered, a plotter of ships' routes

explanation.walkthrough: Prince Henry of Portugal sponsored the early voyages of discovery and is known by a title meaning one who plots a ship's route.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets a ship's courses is a seaman charting the route, and that is the epithet attached to the Portuguese prince.

clue.text: Toiler forced to hang about

indicators.note: forced suggests being pushed into a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker obliged to wait around.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly without purpose, which is what hanging about means.

clue.text: Time to put up sharp note and stamp out

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: acid means sharp or biting
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise a sharp note in music and then stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp note' looks like one musical idea, but sharp and note are separate pieces, and only sharp is put up.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out completely, the same as stamping something out.

clue.text: Man with sense disguises parsimony

indicators.note: a disguise changes the appearance, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensible man hides his stinginess.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme reluctance to spend money, a synonym for being stingy.

clue.text: Drink out of a very old hat

indicators.note: one word lying outside the other means it surrounds it

parts.note: beer is a drink
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Drinking from an ancient hat.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER goes around A and V. 'Old hat' looks like slang for outdated, but it is a literal hat of an old style.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats made of beaver fur were fashionable for centuries, so the animal name also means that kind of headwear.

clue.text: Growin' fruit

parts.note: raising crops is growing them; the apostrophe shows the final G dropped in casual speech

explanation.surface: A folksy word for growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Growin' is the signal: as growing becomes growin', raising becomes raisin' when its G is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapes dried in the sun become these sweet wrinkled morsels, a dried variety of the vine's produce.

clue.text: Shoot leviathan, losing head of harpoon, from side of boat

parts.note: to gun is to shoot

indicators.note: losing the head of a word means its first letter is dropped

parts.note: a leviathan is a sea monster or whale
the opening letter of harpoon

explanation.surface: A whaling scene: firing at a whale from the side of a boat with a harpoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The H removed from WHALE is the first letter of harpoon, leaving WALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side, so it names the side of a vessel.

clue.text: Brought up game bird for plucking

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: tig is the British playground chasing game also called tag
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A game bird raised and then plucked for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird for plucking' sounds like the kitchen, but the plucking is of strings. Tig is the British name for the chasing game tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A gittern is a medieval stringed instrument like a small guitar, played by plucking, so the phrase describes it loosely.

clue.text: A graduate caught with unserviceable calculator

parts.note: taken as written
a Bachelor of Arts
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
US is old slang for useless, short for unserviceable

explanation.surface: A graduate found with a broken calculator.
explanation.walkthrough: US for unserviceable is a crossword convention from service slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic, an ancient calculating device.

clue.text: Report about hard drug

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a report is a loud bang
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A news report about hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside BANG after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is a preparation of cannabis leaves drunk or smoked in India, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Another time, take a profit

parts.note: taken as written
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: Advice to cash in once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more means doing it on a further occasion, so the adverb fits another time.

clue.text: Unjustified belief in education

parts.note: taken as written
tuition is teaching or education

explanation.surface: A sceptic's complaint about faith in schooling that has no basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intuition is a hunch felt without reasoning or evidence, so it is a belief that lacks justification.

clue.text: Cross desert that is all-embracing

indicators.note: embracing something means holding it inside your arms, so it goes in the middle

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: Crossing a desert that stretches out all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand but is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being angry, and irate means very angry, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: It goes all round Land's End

definitions.text: It goes all round Land's End

parts.note: surface reading: the westernmost point of Cornwall, the famous tip of England
setter's reading: where any land ends, at the sea, there is a continuous boundary running all the way around it

explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far tip of Cornwall in England; read lower-case, a land's end is where it meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary between a country and the sea runs right round an island, marking where the ground finishes.

clue.text: The stone for portal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a banded semi-precious mineral
second meaning, read as two words: a doorway or entrance, one gate

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two and it becomes 'a gate', an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a striped variety of chalcedony used in jewellery, and a portal is an entrance, which a gate is.

clue.text: He may have a box at the Palace

definitions.text: He may have a box at the Palace

parts.note: surface reading: a private box at a theatre such as the Palace, or at a sports ground
setter's reading: a guard on duty outside Buckingham Palace, who stands in a little hut

explanation.walkthrough: The Palace Theatre is in London's West End, but here the box is the small wooden shelter a soldier on guard duty stands in.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch at a gate is that kind of guard, and the shelter he stands in is named after him.

clue.text: GIs enter manoeuvres as complete units

indicators.note: manoeuvres move troops into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: American soldiers join war games as whole units of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers are whole numbers, made of complete ones without fractions.
